content.text: : bleeding in quantities too small to be macroscopically observed
: macroscopically observable bleeding w/ accompanying clinical SXS (anemia, tachycardia)
to ligament of Treitz (suspensory muscle of duodenum)
, erosive esophagitis, gastritis/duodenitis, varices, gastric antral vascular ectasia (GAVE)
▪︎Dieulafoy lesion (minor mucosal trauma to an abnormal submucosal artery)
▪︎esophageal cancer, gastric carcinoma, hiatal hernias, Mallory-Weiss syndrome, Boerhaave syndrome
to ligament of Treitz, usually in colon
, IBD, inflammatory diarrhea (EHEC, Shigella, etc.), hemorrhoids
▪︎ischemic colitis, mesenteric ischemia, AV malformation, angiodysplasia
▪︎colorectal carcinoma, colonic polyps, lower abdominal trauma, anorectal trauma
: anemia d/t chronic blood loss, signs of circulatory insufficiency or
hypovolemic shock (tachycardia, hypotension, AMS) in acute hemorrhage
: CBC, CMP, PT/INR, blood type/cross, AST/ALT
» Brisk bleeding: >2cc/min or 1 unit PRBCs q4h
» Slow bleeding: <0.5cc/min or 1 unit PRBCs QD
➀ make patient NPO & insert 2 large-bore IVs
transfuse RBCs, plasma, & platelets in 1:1:1 ratio
